utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [French interpretation coming through on channel 4]. I thank you. It's a good thing I understand you in French because I'm receiving French on the fourth channel. So I think there is a technical problem which can be adjusted very easily. It has happened in the past. So channel 4 should be the English translation. I am no longer hearing French so I take it that the matter has been rectified already. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution? And we are happy to see you back, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and thank you for expressing the concerns regarding my health, also towards the Defence team. Good morning to you, Your Honours and my learned friends on the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben. And good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear on behalf of Mr. Naser Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. Good morning to our colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries before we bring in the new witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you both. Let's get the witness in. Ms. Vidovic, has he been informed that he will be here on Monday at least, possibly even Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, while the witness is being brought in I understand from a brief conversation with Mr. Jones outside of court earlier today he expects he will be either two days or perhaps the lion's share of two days. If that be so I would prefer to start my cross-examination on the Monday, if that of course is convenient to the Trial Chamber. And, of course, if he doesn't finish very early tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we can hear your comments on this. You know how much you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I think I'll be about two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: About two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The estimate is five hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Two full sittings would be three hours and a half plus three hours and a half. That's seven hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes but the estimate was five hours and I think it's going to be more like six hours. That's why I say two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In that case, unless things take a different turning than expected, which sometimes happens, and the cross-examination finishes very early tomorrow, then of course we will start the cross-examination on Monday, but do I take it also that you intend to finish your cross-examination on Monday? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, there is a lot of exhibits in the Defence Exhibit list. You know that I honestly hope to finish it on Monday but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm just asking for an indication from you because when you told me -- for the time being the witness can sit down. MR. DI FAZIO: My prediction is, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's heard me. MR. DI FAZIO: My prediction Your Honour is that I will take all of Monday at the very least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Monday is the 12th or the 13th? The 12th, yeah. Monday is the 12th. So we have scheduled this witness to be here up to the 13th. So if Mr. Di Fazio doesn't finish on Monday we are still within -- it won't disrupt our schedule for next week.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then I can comfortably tell you, unless my colleagues disagree with me, that chances are that we will say, okay, start on Monday. All right? I mean, do keep in mind, I've been making assessments as we go along and this last witness, for example, the time taken by the Prosecution excluding the re-examination -- by the Defence, excluding the re-examination, and the Prosecution has been exactly the same, just two minutes difference. So if you need two days, I wouldn't be surprised if we are going to have -- find ourselves with you taking another two days. This is an important witness, there is no question about it. All right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Buric, could you stand up, please? Good morning to you, Mr. Buric. I take it that you are receiving interpretation in your own language of what I'm --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- saying. Good. If at any time between now and when you finish your testimony next week there are problems with interpretation, in other words if you are not receiving interpretation in your own language or if the volume -- sound level is too high or too low then please draw your attention straight away and we will rectify the matter immediately. Welcome to this Tribunal. And also welcome to this case which has been instituted against Naser Oric. You have been summoned as a witness by the Defence and very soon you will start giving evidence. Our rules require that before you do so, you make a solemn declaration, something which is equivalent to an oath in some domestic jurisdictions and the essence, the substance of the solemn declaration, is an undertaking on your part that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of the solemn declaration is going to be handed to you now by Madam Usher. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us that you will be testifying the truth. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Buric. Please make yourself comfortable. I will explain very briefly what's going to happen. Since you have been summoned as a Defence witness, it is one of the lawyers conducting the Defence of Mr. Oric that will be examining you in chief. This time it is Mr. Jones, I take it, whom I with will imagine you have already met and discussed things. The examination-in-chief is expected to last today and tomorrow but it could also go longer. After that, we will start with your cross-examination, and it is Mr. Di Fazio, the gentleman who is nearest to you on your right from the Prosecution team that will be cross-examining you. Again, the cross-examination may last from one up to two days. So you're anticipated to be still here testifying on Tuesday of the coming week. I take it you are already -- you have already been made aware of that. In between sessions and in between sittings, and especially since you are going to be here the weekend, you are required not to communicate, not to communicate, with anyone nor -- or neither to let anyone communicate with you on matters that are related to your testimony or to the events that happened in the territory of ex-Yugoslavia upon which you will be testifying. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It doesn't mean that you need to remain incommunicado, that you cannot, for example, ring up members of your family or that you cannot receive calls from family members or friends. It doesn't mean that. It just means that you're not to discuss these things with anyone. Now, my name is Carmel Agius, I am the Presiding Judge in this case and I come from the Mediterranean island of Malta. To my right I have Judge Hans Henrik Brydensholt from the Kingdom of Denmark. And to my left I have Judge Professor Albin Eser from Germany. Together we compose this Trial Chamber and we will make sure that the procedure is adhered to and that you will be able to give your testimony in full. One short advice, but an important one, that I would like to give you is that don't fall into the temptation of giving -- of providing more evidence -- more information than you are being asked to do. If you get a question that can be answered by a yes and a no, it does not need any further elucidation or explanation on your part, then answer it by a mere yes or a no. Don't volunteer more information than is required from you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. We are not here to hear the entire history of the events in Yugoslavia but only to hear your evidence in relation to the questions that are put to you. Now, there will be questions from the Defence and there will be questions from the Prosecution. Your responsibility pursuant to the solemn declaration that you have made is to answer all questions truthfully and fully and to the best of your ability irrespective of who is putting the question to you. Have I made myself clear to you? Do you have any questions before we start with your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is all clear to me. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much for your cooperation, Mr. Buric, and Mr. Jones now will start with his direct. Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Jones:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning from me, too, Mr. Buric.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we start by you please giving the Court your full name?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Nesib Buric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it right that you were born on the 18th of October, 1963?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were born in Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which municipality Osmace is in?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Osmace are within the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is it right that you were married in 1989 in Brezani?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I got married in Brezani in 1989.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you have three children, a girl born in Tuzla, in 1997 and twin boys born in 2000?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it also right that your family were not with you during the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: It is true. My wife was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Finally as far as your education is concerned can you confirm that you went to primary school in Osmace and then in OSAT graduating in 1977 -- sorry, in 1978?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to high school in Srebrenica and graduated in 1981?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that in 1981 you enrolled in a teacher training programme, graduating in 1986?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it right that from 1987 to 1992, you were employed as a maths and physics teacher at the primary school in Brezani?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, after the war, is it right that you worked in the municipality of Srebrenica in the field of education?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you retired in the year 2000 and you currently live in Tuzla? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were born in Osmace. Did you grow up there?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were you there at the start of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have a new exhibit of a map. In our never-ending search for the perfect map we have a map which is larger than the ones we have been looking at so far but we think that might assist. So if copies could be distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest that this be left if the proximity of the witness because I take it that we will be making use of it --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- as we go along, instead of having to go -- take it to and fro.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. If I could also request that the witness use this pen? It's a bit thinner than the ones which have been used before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could take a moment, Mr. Buric, to familiarise yourself with the map and then locate Osmace, and please circle it. Thank you. Now, you've circled Osmace, the words Osmace and then you've drawn a larger circle. Can you explain the significance of those two circles?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Osmace are a somewhat larger settlement with five or six adjacent hamlets, those being Mahali, Hadrovici, Ostrana, Secimici, Marsalovic, and Prisoj, six hamlets plus Osmace is the entire village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us, before the war, what was the ethnic composition of the village of Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Osmace were 100 per cent Muslim. It used to have about 1.000 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the nearest Serb village to Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: The nearest Serb village is the village of Brezani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you locate that, please, on the map and circle it?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you circled the larger settlement of Brezani just there?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Brezani are an ethnically pure Serb village consisting of three to four units, Turija, Primorac, and the main one being Brezani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was the approximate population of Brezani before the war?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: According to the old administrative organisation, Osmace and Brezani were together in the local commune of Brezani so the Muslims were in the majority up to 80 per cent, the remaining 20 were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So in the area that you've circled on the map for Brezani, roughly how many inhabitants would there be before the war?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Before the war, there were about 50 households, around 200 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far away is Brezani from Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Brezani are about five kilometres away from Osmace, four to five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from Osmace, if you're standing in Osmace, can you see what's going on in the village of Brezani?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes, very clearly. As the crow flies, it is less than 1.000 or 1500 metres, between Osmace and Brezani, with certain depressions in between. So four to five kilometres by road and as the crow flies, around 1500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before the war, were there any sort of military facilities in Brezani?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. In Brezani, there was the conscription centre for the reserve force are of the former JNA and the TO was trained there, the TO of the Srebrenica municipality. There were trenches and fortifications, and the infrastructure including a school, the old school, where the reserve forces used to be accommodated when they were being trained in Brezani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've confirmed that before the war, you were a school teacher. Where exactly were you teaching?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: The school was between Osmace and Brezani n the location of Pazaric. It is not marked on the map, but I will try to point to the approximate location where the school was. Next to Secimici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now I want to take you to 1991, 1992, when the wars in the former Yugoslavia were starting. Did you hear any talk at the school about the outbreak of war in the former Yugoslavia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the conflict broke out in Croatia in 1991, the Serb children from the primary school at Brezani left school en masse and they were sent to schools in Serbia, Bajina Basta, Lazarjevic [phoen], Cacak, because the Serb population of the village of Brezani mostly had houses in Serbia, 99 per cent of them did, and we suddenly realised that their conscripts were all leaving for the battle grounds in Croatia and the Serb children used to tell about it to the Muslim children, either because they didn't know that they shouldn't say anything or because they wanted to boast, but -- well, that's how we had the information as to what was going on in the village of Brezani as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And in Brezani you told us that before the war, that there were TO were trained there and that there was a JNA conscription centre. Did you hear at any time talk about the JNA taking the weapons of the TO?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the conflict broke out in Croatia, all weapons from the Territorial Defence were taken by the JNA and distributed to the Serb population, not just in Srebrenica but all over Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if local Serbs, Serbs in your area, received weapons from the JNA which had taken those weapons from the TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did they have to be weapons taken from the TO, Mr. Jones? Or any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was talking specifically with the TO but indeed receiving weapons would also function for my purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Require them as being identified as being TO weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, the source isn't that important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the question clear or should I repeat it? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You better repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if local Serbs in your area at this time that we are discussing were receiving weapons from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Most weapons that were taken from the TO were distributed to the local Serb population. Those were slightly outdated weapons, such as M-48 rifles, mortars, old weapons that was in the hands of the TO. By the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, was distributed to the Serb population, and we also had some papers on which it was stated that back in 1976 also the Serb population was being given weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from the weapons from the TO which were distributed to the Serbs, did you ever become aware of local Serbs receiving other weapons, newer weapons?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. They -- as they withdrew, the JNA from Slovenia and Croatia, they were bringing new weapons, automatic rifles, PMs and 84 machine-guns, and the artillery weapons for the most part consisted of mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the interests of statement we are not going to dwell on the background to the conflict in Bosnia. I'm going to take you straight to the beginning of 1992. At that time, did you notice any goings on in Brezani?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. In the beginning of 1992, as I've already mentioned, Serbs were giving weapons, and they started organising neighbourhood watches or -- and they all went into training at Brezani and in other places, so those activities were already underway in the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Just dealing firstly with Brezani, is that something, the training you've mentioned, is that something you can actually see with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Brezani is between Muslim villages where villagers passing by could see them on training, at playgrounds, for example at the playground next to the school in Brezani, could you see it from the nearby villages with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you've mentioned seeing Serbs in a neighbourhood watch, I think it was -- the term was interpreted as, anyway. Did you see what the people that were the Serbs who were conducting this local watch, what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. All able-bodied Serbs who had gone through the military training had the JNA camouflage uniforms, all those from the Territorial Defence of the former Yugoslavia and necessary basically the same uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said they were training in Brezani and other places. What other places did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had information, according to which the Serbs in that part of the territory Podrinje, were organising active training in Jezero, Brezani, Skelani and the main training centre was at Ruljevici next to Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I think it's not actually marked on the map but if you can locate it and mark it with an R, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the names of the villages are extremely important to us. Perhaps the witness could repeat them since they have not been included in the transcript correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Brezani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Brezani we have already marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Ruljevici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ruljevici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he also mentioned Skelani.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Jezero?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: And the main centre at Jezero. So it is in eastern Podrinje, the eastern part of the municipality of Srebrenica. All these places are in that area, Jezero, Skelani, Fakovici and Ruljevici. Fakovici and Ruljevici are part of the municipality of Bratunac. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps to assist Mr. Jones, perhaps we could have something to designate one from the other, perhaps an R or a J.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was about to ask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we give an R for Ruljevici, I think the other locations are actually marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you direct the witness straight. Let's take them one by one. Can you direct him to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So he knows where Fakovici is and one moment, I want to make sure --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, could you circle Fakovici, please?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it right that the -- thank you. And the area which you've marked with an R, is that Ruljevici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ruljevici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Further up and not further down. No, no, that's further down. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's just at the left of Vranesevici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the old school used to be and it was closed down by the Serbs two years previously and it was turned into a training centre for the Serb population. It is an ethnically Serb village so the surrounding villages around Ruljevici were Serb villages as well. So Muslims did not have much of an insight into what they were up to. It was about three kilometres away from Grabovacka Rijeka and Grabovacka Rijeka is about three kilometres away from Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could we go down on the monitor no where he -- one moment, that's number 8. That's Jezero he's marked over there. Okay. And any other markings that he has made.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think that's fine. Yes. Skelani has also been marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to some of these locations shortly. Sticking with Ruljevici for the moment. What you've just told us about it being a centre for training, what's your basis for that information?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We had the exact information because the delegation of the municipality of Srebrenica, since there had been tensions in the Zvijezda area in the beginning of 1992, February, March or so, and a delegation from the municipality of Srebrenica went up there to see what was going on, but on their way back from Skelani, through Fakovici, either on purpose or not, they went through this place called Ruljevici and I was told about this by a man called Hasan, and the president of the municipality of Srebrenica at the time, Basina Basovic [phoen] was present as well, and they told me how they saw all those garden there were soldiers, Serb soldiers wearing military olive drab uniforms, and so those people were inhabitants from the surrounding Serb villages who were going through this training and they all went through at least one or two weeks' training in those centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In what period are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: February, March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information about the numbers of people who were in training -- who had been through training or who had been trained in Ruljevici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: They supposed that there could have been about 300 participants at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify one thing in the transcript, you mentioned there had been tensions in what the Zvijezda area in the beginning of 1992. Is that correct? Did you say the Zvijezda area?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Lijesce area. It's near Skelani. The municipality is Skelani and the hamlet is Lijesce, and there were some tensions there between the Muslim and the Serb population and so a delegation from the municipality of Srebrenica went up there to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you spell Lijesce, please, for the transcript?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: L-I-J-E-S-C-E.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I see you're locating that on the map, and if you could mark that with an L.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: [Marks] It's about three to four kilometres away from Skelani in the direction of Bujakovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Buric, could you put an L near the first marking. And what's the other one that you put further up on top of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's from Skelani in the direction of Bujakovici. It's south of Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's Bujakovici which is the other area that's been circled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago we were discussing the arming of local Serbs with weapons. Were you aware of any time of weapons being brought into the area, into the Brezani area, by any conveyance?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. They -- we got the information from a number of people from the children, in fact, that people who had trucks were bringing weapons into those villages. The main supplier of weapons for Brezani was a Milajko Krtajic [phoen], Raso Orasanin, and the sons of somebody who was called Milivoje. I don't know his family name, so it was a guy called Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Milivoje, and his sons had trucks and they were the main arms suppliers for the area of Brezani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you receive any information as to where these trucks were coming from?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. All weapons came from the direction of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were trucks the only conveyances that were used to bring weapons into the area or were you aware of other means?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. When they no longer felt that that line, Skelani-Brezani, was safe, they started getting weapons from Fakovici en masse and the transport took place on horse back, and by roundabout mountain roads from Fakovici to Brezani and also by JNA helicopters. So they were flying over the area, the helicopters, I mean, the JNA helicopters, marked by a red cross, in fact. They were flying across to Bosnia from Serbia and it was something we could see with the naked eye from where we were in Osmace. We could see very clearly from where those helicopters were coming from. And so it was for Brezani, Ratkovici and Ducici because there was a corps commander at the time who was a guy called Zivanovic and he was from the village of Ducici. I think he was the commander of Drina Corps or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've mentioned Ducici and Ratkovici and you said so it was for Brezani, Ratkovici, and Ducici. What do you mean by that, precisely, that the weapons were being delivered to those areas? Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Weapons were being delivered to those Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: To me it's not very clear evidence; Mr. Jones may wish to clarify it. The witness said, talking about the influx of weapons, that there were helicopters, and then said so it was for Brezani, Ratkovici, and Ducici, because there was a corps commander at the time, and it's not quite clear if there is any link between the influx of weapons and the corps commander and if so, where was the corps commander and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair comment. Yes, Mr. Jones, could you address this. MR. DI FAZIO: And perhaps of course the occasion as well, if there is any time on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly can you say when this was approximately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's mark them first of all on the map so that we -- we know already where they are, but let the witness mark Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Ducici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Ducici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mark it please on the map.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. So this is Ratkovici. I just marked it. And within the area of Ratkovici, a smaller area is Ducici. And let me clarify this, if I may. The commander who was in Knin, he was the commander of the Serb armed forces in Knin and he was born in Ducici so he was originally from there and he was arming his own village. He was not a commander in that area. Later on, when he came from the Krajina area he became commander of the Drina Corps in Zvornik but he was not a local commander at the time. He was a commander in Knin but when Krajina fell, he came to the area of Zvornik and he was a commander of the Serb Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the time he was arming the people of his village, of Ducici, in other words, at the time, what was -- what was he doing? Was he still in the Krajina in Knin, in Croatia, or not? In the Croatian Krajina or had he already come back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He was in Krajina. He was at the battlefield there, and it was in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That is clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear it was in April 1992 that this was going on, the arming of Ducici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever find out how many weapons had been delivered to the Serbs in that area, in Ducici, Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We noticed helicopters at least on four or five occasions, a helicopter that was delivering weapons. And as to quantities, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as Brezani is concerned, you've told us that that was nearby and could you see what's going on there. What's the source of your information apart from seeing helicopters that the weapons were specifically reaching Ducici and Ratkovici? Did you ever any other source of information?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: There were rumours in the surrounding Muslim villages that they saw that weapons were delivered to Ducici by helicopters from Fakovici, and as to Brezani, we knew that they were getting weapons and that those weapons were being transported on horse back from Fakovici, weapons and ammunition, that is, and they went through the forests and creeks, et cetera, in a roundabout way anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you refer to the surrounding Muslim villages, which villages would those be, the villages which surrounded Ducici and Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: There are Muslim villages around Ducici and Ratkovici. They are Poznanovici, Podkorjen, and Dedici. But on the other side, to the north, there are other villages called Mocevici, Dimnici, and Brezovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you refer to receiving information or of hearing rumours from Muslims in villages around Ratkovici and Ducici, which villages did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Poznanovici, Dedici, and Podkorjen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any incident at any stage which signalled to you that the war in Bosnia had begun in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. The beginning of war-like conflict or something that triggered off a large scale panic amongst the population in the area of Srebrenica started on the occasion of the murder of two Muslim citizens, Osmanovic, Bahrudin and Hrvac Meho on the 13th and 14th of April and it happened at Vitez. They went to Bajina Basta, they bought fuel, and they were on their way back, and then those guys who were in training at Jezero basically massacred those two Muslims. So it was at Vitez. As you go from Jezero to Kragljivoda, it is about five -- four to five kilometres away. It's not marked on the map so I'm going to mark it myself. So here is Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. It is slightly closer to Kragljivoda than to Jezero, the site of the murder, that is. So it is only two kilometres away from Kragljivoda, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the record you've marked Vitez with a V. You mentioned these two people who were killed. Did you actually see the bodies of either one or the other of them?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. On that day, or, rather, on the day after, I was going to the petrol station at Bajina Basta because there was a shortage of fuel in the area. So I was on my way to Bajina Basta that and I went past that location and I didn't notice anything amiss. When I got to my mother-in-law's house at Dobrak she told me that during the night two Muslims had been killed in the Vitez area. I returned home immediately with my family, and I knew what the place was and I was driving slowly and I saw it. I mean, I stepped out of my car and I saw Bahrudin Osmanovic's body and I didn't see Meho's body because it was thrown into the woods, a bit further down, about ten metres down, and something that struck me, and I'm never going to be able to forget this, it was a completely massacred body and he was wearing yellow boots and so on his -- his left leg he had a boot and on the right leg, there was just a white plastic bag. So I didn't have it in me to do anything more so I turned back and I got into my car and I went in the direction of Osmace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did the news of those deaths have any effect on the Muslim inhabitants in the area?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: In that part of Podrinje, the murders of Meho and Bahrudin triggered off such a huge panic and chaos amongst the Muslim population that masses of people started leaving and they started going away to Slovenia, to Germany, in the direction of Tuzla, but at the time the problem was that most people were unable to leave because there wasn't enough fuel, they didn't have any transport; they couldn't leave. And that's how they withdrew into themselves, into their own villages, and they were kind of lying low in those villages, just making sure they protected their lives because they knew of those units that were at Jezero and Muslims had no weapons and there was an overall panic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken about units that were at Jezero, could you. Can you just elaborate on that a little bit? What were you referring to there?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: On that day when I was coming back from Bajina Basta, I saw personally at Jezero a group of Serbs that was undergoing training, and there may have been 30 to 50 people there. They were wearing olive drab uniforms, that is the upper part was olive drab, and they wore civilian pants, so rather their shirts only were of military nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what day was this, please?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: I believe that was the 14th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at this time, were you aware of what was going on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in Srebrenica? Around this time, the middle of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become aware of the fact that Srebrenica was taken over by the Serbs in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We received information, I don't know whether it was on the 18th or the 19th of April, and when the -- these two lads were killed, there was general chaos in the municipality. People withdrew in the larger Muslim villages and the town remained empty. And the Serbs from Bratunac, the -- Arkan's men, and the White Eagles, came from the region of Sase and Potocari and entered the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: If I may add, whatever they found on their way, and the Muslim people, they found there including the elderly and the handicapped, they killed them, I don't know the exact number but there were about 50 people killed in Srebrenica and they torched the main street. This was the Petrici street, there were about 100 houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is likely that I'll be on me feet rather often. I apologise but I have to -- the transcript is incorrect. The witness said -- or rather, the witness didn't say that on the 18th or 19th of April, these two men were killed. But that he received the information on the events in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were killed between the 13th and the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And he said that the information about the events in Srebrenica was received by him on the 18th or the 19th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Do you confirm that, Mr. Buric? Do you confirm the correction that Madam Vidovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were telling us about how you learned that in Srebrenica about 50 people had been killed, this is in April 1992 and that about a hundred houses in Petrici were torched. Did you hear of any other goings on in Srebrenica when it was taken over by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else did you hear?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We heard that from the people that were fleeing, the people who managed to flee on the 18th or the 19th, and withdraw towards the villages, and they told us that there was a state of general chaos in Srebrenica, that the Serbs began robbing Muslim houses, businesses, and that anything of any value was being taken away from Srebrenica, driven away on trucks, that businesses are being torched. In those five or six days, anything that was of value in Srebrenica was taken away, plundered, taken away by trucks or destroyed, or killed for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in terms of being taken away by trucks is that something which you yourself saw?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Osmace and Brezani, that's relatively close, and one can see the other place with the naked eye and we saw this massive arrival of trucks and we supposed that they were plundering the property in Srebrenica and from the industrial area of Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see on the map that there is a road clearly between Srebrenica and Skelani. How far is Osmace from that road?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Osmace are about 2 kilometres away from the road Srebrenica-Skelani. But from Osmace, one can see the road. Some 2 to 3 kilometres of it can be seen with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this time, mid-April 1992, did you see any traffic on that road?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Since the population withdrew and didn't move about freely, because of the murders that triggered off panic and fear, people didn't leave their homes, didn't go -- want to go far, as much as 100 metres, and they saw Serb trucks that passed by for days, taking away stolen goods, so we are talking about military personnel, people in uniforms. They were all equipped and they used trucks and passenger cars to take away everything from Srebrenica and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I think you've referred already to an area called Kragljivoda. Could you please locate that on the map and mark the area of Kragljivoda?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. It is marked here Kragljivoda in blue letters. It is an overpass, in the mountains, and there were no immediate settlements there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know a village called Gladovici?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is that part or not of the Kragljivoda area?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Not a part of Kragljivoda, but it is adjacent to it. It is perhaps 3 to 5 kilometres away from Kragljivoda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Ilijaz Pilav?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he's from?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: From Gladovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned this traffic of these Serb military vehicles on the road between Srebrenica and Skelani. Did the people of Osmace or the people in Kragljivoda do anything about that?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Muslims couldn't use that road for days. They couldn't -- and didn't dare to use the road. The property was being taken towards Skelani. A group of young men from Gladovici observed that and they were also in Osmace and they saw that on the 7th of May a Serb bus with soldiers and several trucks departed and on the 6th or the 7th they torched Ljeskovik and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they torched Ljeskovik who are you referring to, and Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Those were Muslim villages and it was done by the Serbs in Skelani. They went to Ljeskovik and Zeleni Jadar that were Muslim villages, perhaps 150 houses were there, and on the 7th of May, they torched the Muslim villages of Ljeskovik, Zeleni Jadar, and they killed everyone that was left behind but was unable -- who was unable to flee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read an extract from a book titled "War Hospitals." I'd like in fact since it's only in English, I won't put it in front of the witness but it's D199, "War Hospital," and the page reference is page 44, page 45. I'm going to read an extract from this book War Hospital by Dr. Sheri Fink, which is an exhibit in this case. Just for our benefit, page 44 sets the time and the place. Mid-April 1992. Vladovici and then it's page 45, second paragraph. I'll just read. It says, "In the mornings, Ilijaz and a few friends hiked up the nearby hill, Kalina [phoen], to give themselves a view of the single paved road that wound southeast from Srebrenica toward the Bosnian border town of Skelani and ultimately across the bridge to Serbia." Pausing there, do you know the hill, Kalina?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you locate and circle that on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've heard this reference to this single paved road. Is that the road which you referred to earlier from Srebrenica to Skelani? Is that a single paved road?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, carrying on it says, "From the hill top, they watched Serb military patrols pass back and forth and saw tendrils of smoke, first white, then dark, rise and bloom like flowers over the graves of Bosnian Muslim villages to the southeast. They witnessed lines of villages stumbling into Gladovici bent beneath hastily packed bundles of possessions, searching for refuge from the Serb nationalist soldiers they called Chetniks." Now, you've told us you saw these Serb military patrols on that road in April 1992. I want to ask you, firstly, did that have any effect on communications or contacts between the people in Osmace and Gladovici on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We are therefore still talking about April and the beginning of May. There was no possibility for Osmace to communicate with any other Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And now staying with this passage which I read out, the language is somewhat poetical but it refers to smoke rising over the graves of Bosnian Muslim villages. Do you know what that would refer to, which villages?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Ljeskovik and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the reference to villagers with packs on their backs stumbling into Gladovici seeking refuge from Chetniks, can you explain what you would understand by that passage referring to events in April and May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: It's the 7th of May of 1992. When Ljeskovik and Zeleni Jadar, the two Muslim villages were torched, the people from there fled into the woods, and those who managed reached the Muslim villages of Karacici, Gladovici, or Urisici, but people mainly fled in all directions from these Muslim villages. Those who were unable to were later killed. They killed the elderly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'll move down past the passage referring to the lack of organisation in Osmace of resistance to the second-to-last paragraph, "On May 6, Ilijaz climbed Kalina hill with several of his neighbours. They looked down and watched a military truck moving slowly along the Srebrenica-Skelani road. The idea of ambushing enemy vehicles Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. had tantalised the men for days, using the element of surprise, that was a way the weak could fight the strong." And then the book then goes on to recount an ambush that took place and which is described on page 46. Are you familiar with an ambush taking place on that road?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. I participated in that ambush myself. Kalina was on one side of the road, looking from the river to the left, and Osmace are to the right of the river. So we looked on from Osmace. Across from us as the crow flies about five to six kilometres away was Ljeskovik. Zeleni Jadar couldn't be seen but one could see Ljeskovik, and, in the morning, 7.00 or 8.00 in the morning, the bus departed together with two trucks full of Serb soldiers. They went to that place and we were observing it throughout and they torched Ljeskovik and Zeleni Jadar. We decided to have an ambush on the right side, to open fire on the convoy, but on the left side, independently from us, the people, the boys from Gladovici did the same. When the two trucks were coming back, we opened fire, as well as the -- a Mercedes vehicle that was with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people from Osmace were involved in this ambush?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: There were only five boys from Osmace.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction: Nine boys from Osmace.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And in total there may have been 18 to 19 people from Gladovici and Osmace together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was anyone killed from Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: That day when we opened fire, despite of our fear, but we fled immediately and then two people from Osmace were killed, Ismet Krdzic and Zijad Delic, and then the Serbs moved on towards Skelani, and later on, a Niva jeep came as well as the bus, and then the trucks and the Mercedes vehicle, they all went in a convoy towards Skelani and we had two dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We saw the phrase there, "using the element of surprise, that was a way the weak could fight the strong." Would you care to comment on that passage?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: This was the type of resistance by the population that could no longer simply stand by, because we were the next in line to be torched or killed. The first village to the west closest to the Drina and Serbia was the one that was torched first. They torched Ljeskovik and Zeleni Jadar. The next would have been Karic [phoen] and then Osmace. We couldn't simply stand by. The village of Osmace had 21 hunting rifles as well as several rifles kept by some members of the reserve forces, and some pieces of arms were actually purchased. In the ambush there were six or seven pieces of arms. But the Serbs, there were probably around 100 of them so six or seven boys on the other side could do nothing. We tried to use the surprise factor in order to seize or try to seize some weapons and to prevent further torching and plundering.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in the village of Osmace you had 21 hunting rifles. I think you told us that there were about a thousand inhabitants of Osmace. So is it right, then, one in 50 people had a rifle of some description?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you now, please, to look at an exhibit, a new exhibit. The ERN number is 04367573. And just for the record it's a document from the command of the Skelani Independent Battalion dated 25 October 1993. Battalion history and wartime record since the formation of the Drina Corps, and it's to the Drina Corps command, forward to the first Birac Brigade. Now, firstly, is it right, Mr. Buric, that I showed you that document when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a moment to peruse it. I'm going to read two highlighted sections. Firstly in the first paragraph, and it's starting from the second sentence, "On 18 April 1992, in addition to village guards, a company strong unit counting 120 men was established in the school in Jezero and seven-day trainings began." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you were telling us in terms of Serb units and activity at Jezero?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This proves that they actively underwent training at Jezero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then it goes on, "First combat operations were carried out on [illegible] May 1992 when the unit marched along the Jezero-Stolac axis and fired artillery at Osmace in response to the Muslim ambush of 6 May 1992 set up below Osmace village in which five Serbian civilians were killed." Now, I'll ask you about the shelling of Osmace in a minute. But were any Serb civilians to your knowledge killed in the ambush of which we've spoken?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: As I said a minute ago, that we opened fire and fled. No one was killed on their side and we had two killed. They fired back of course, with everything they had from the two trucks, and from the Mercedes. Therefore, not a single civilian was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, just pausing from that document for a moment, I'm going to refer to war hospital and it's page 46 and the second to last paragraph, I'll just read it, "The groups shot at trucks and they shot at cars, killing a number of Serbs. Ilijaz and his men insisted that they killed only soldiers who returned fire. Indeed, two attackers in Osmace also died, but Serbs in the area told a different story, that seven Serb civilians, including two women, were killed." So do I take it from what you said that as far as you know, there is no truth in the claim that Serb civilians were killed in that ambush?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: There were no civilians. They were in military uniforms. And concerning the soldiers, we didn't see any Serb soldiers killed. The trucks came and then went further towards Skelani. The only people that were left there were our two dead men without weapons and they didn't even have weapons prior to that. They simply came as observers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now going back to this document in front of you, I'm going to read a second section, the second paragraph, where it says, "The battalion first company was in the Jezero village sector and organised flexible defence. The second company held its positions along the Kusici-Gradina-Cosici-Bojakovici line. The third company held positions on the Konjuv-Donji Zljebac line. The following villages were mopped up in this period: Velika and Mala Daljegosta, Lijesce, Zabokvica, Gumci, Dobrak, Barakovici, Zgunja, Kadrici, Pajici Peci, and Bukovik, and Trubari." Now, do you know the villages mentioned there?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. When the incident at Osmace took place, and when those boys went, the Serb boys went on towards Skelani, their battalion, I don't know how many soldiers there were in it, perhaps 500 to 600. It went out and they went into Muslim villages, Velika Daljegosta, Mala Daljegosta, Lijesce, Skelani, Resagici, Dobrak, Bljecova [phoen] -- sorry, not Bljecova. Zgunja, Barakovici, Bukovik, Trubari. They torched in total over 2.000 houses on the 7th of May, and they killed everyone they found there. Everyone who was unable to flee into the woods. And they took the cattle away and plundered the houses, and then they torched them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these villages which we see in this document being referred to as being mopped up, those were all Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: They were all Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask for an exhibit number, please, for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, before we give this document an exhibit number, we also need to give an exhibit number to the map. So let's start with the map, please. D7 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D737, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 737. And the document that in B/C/S has ERN number 04367573 and the corresponding English translation of same, being marked as Defence Exhibit D738. I think we can have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, may I ask one question just before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any Muslim villages in the Skelani area spared this mopping up?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. All villages along the River Drina, all Muslim villages, starting with Mala Daljegosta, that is furthest to the east, all along the river to Kragljivoda, were torched. I'm referring to more than 2.000 houses that were torched on that day. And dozens of people who were infirm or disabled or had not managed to escape for whatever reason were killed. They were set alight alive, and they were thrown on to haystacks and rubbers, rubber tires, et cetera, and they were set on fire and entire families were thrown on to those fires.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a 30-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break, Mr. Buric, you were describing the burning of Muslim villages in the Skelani area. Do you know whether the Serbs who were involved in those operations were local Serbs or were Serbs from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. outside the area or both?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We obtained information in the beginning, in the beginning of May, we obtained information that there were local Serbs as well as volunteers coming back from the battlefields in Croatia. They used to help them on a regular basis. They were people who had gone through training, a broader type of training, and people who were sowing terror in Croatia, they would come back from the battlefields over there and come to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, if a Serb living in this area in early 1992 were to say that no Muslims were forcibly expelled from their homes, that the Muslims decided of their own will to go and live in the woods, would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. Who would choose to live in the woods, and abandon their homes and -- their ancestral homes? No absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And answer this only if you can. Knowing the area, the lay of the land, people, the culture, do you think anyone expressing that view could be expressing an honestly held belief?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain this a little bit? Because the question is not all that clear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put this a different way. Knowing the area, as you do, do you think any Serb living there in 1992 could be ignorant of what was going on in these Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: I claim with a great deal of certainty that all Serbs knew what as going on and what was being prepared for months and months in the end of 1991, throughout 1992, and then in 1993. I can state that every single Serb knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The smoke from burning Muslim villages, is that something you could see personally with your own eyes in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: The entire population, let me reiterate this, the entire population of the Drina valley that was torched on the 7th of May was taking to the woods, and three or four days later, they would come to my village, Osmace, to Miholjevine, to Podkorjen, and they were coming through the woods trying to avoid Serb ambushes because they had patrols in those forests as well, and then they would eventually get to our village and we took them in. At one point in my village, Osmace, there were 3 or four times more refugees than the local population, the number of the local population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can rephrase --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt you but, as I say, he gave us the information but he didn't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just specifically on whether it was visible that Muslim villages were burning on the 7th of May 1992, is that something you can confirm or not?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a great deal of smoke. You could see it quite clearly. And so basically, we saw it around Jezero. It was easy to see. You could see Jezero and Bukovik burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a man called Branislav Gligic?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We had heard that this terror that was being spread around Skelani was the work of the brother, Gligici, and somebody called Zivko who used to be a police officer from Skelani, from the Skelani police station, and I think he was a chief of police. I think he was appointed chief of police in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You referred to the brothers, Gligic. Do you know their names, first names?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they are from?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: We know that they are from Skelani, and the population that was on the run, that was fleeing the area, they identified them and they told us about those three people that I've just mentioned, that they were the ring leaders in all of that. When Mala Daljegosta, Velika Daljegosta, and Tursunovici, three Muslim villages were emptied basically of populace and the entire population was transferred to either Serbia or Macedonia, those three people were leading the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'm going back to War Hospital very briefly. It's not necessary for us all necessarily to have it in front of us. It's just one sentence, page 49, the first paragraph, and referring still to the people in the Kragljivoda area, it says, "Ilijaz's neighbour, the minaret builder Sefik Mandzic came to lead the 'troops.'" Troops in inverted commas Did you someone called Sefik Mandzic?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Sefik Mandzic was an inhabitant of Gladovici. He led no troops. He was a somewhat more courageous man and together with those five or six guys from the area of Gladovici, he fired at those trucks. But there were no troops whatsoever. They were just four to five people with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Sefik Mandzic survive the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. Sefik was killed on the 5th of October 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was he killed?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Sefik Mandzic was killed on the road from Jagodinja to Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Or Vladijovici [phoen] in that area. The Muslim village of Jagodnja was torched and he went there to help and then he stepped on a landmine in a forest and that's how he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I'm going to come back to that later. Have you heard of Nedzad Bektic?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where he's from?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: I do. He's from a place called Karacici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was he ever involved in organising the resistance in Kragljivoda, resistance to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. He went to a military academy and he came to the area much, much later but the organiser of the defence at Kragljivoda was Mandzic, Sefik, and throughout that period, he was a local leader of that resistance, of a local group, up until his death in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask if the witness could be shown P75, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you will see this document dated 26 May 1992, refers among other things to, quote, "Nedzad Bektic from Karacici being a member of the Srebrenica TO staff, organiser of armed resistance in the area of Kragljivoda." Now would it be true to say on 26 May 1992 that Nedzad Bektic was "the organiser of armed resistance in the area of Kragljivoda"?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. The organiser of resistance, and the leader of the Kragljivoda group, was Sefik Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says that Bektic is from Karacici. What municipality is Karacici in?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Karacici is in the municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's referring to a village in the municipality of Srebrenica. This document refers to Atif Krdzic from Srebrenica. To your knowledge, was Atif Krdzic from Srebrenica, as this document claims?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. Atif Krdzic is from Osmace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a house in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. He had a house in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Senahid Tabakovic. To your knowledge, was he from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. He is from Stozersko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In light of the answers you've just given, would you see this document as a reliable source of information?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: This document is definitely not a reliable source of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd ask if the witness could now be shown P4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document is dated 15th of June 1992. And it refers to all the TOs which will be organised, i.e. in the future, to be organised. And it refers to the Osmace TO among others, Territorial Defence. Did your men in Osmace ever call yourselves or at least in June 1992, did you call yourself the Osmace Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: No. I never heard this term Territorial Defence. It was a group from Osmace, the Osmace group, encompassing all those hamlets that we've mentioned before, Mahala and the others, and I never heard the term Territorial Defence. It was a resistance organised by the population. There were no military units of any sort. It is simply about the population organising a resistance movement in the village of Osmace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And well, I won't labour the point about Nedzad Bektic but again we see that apparently he's charged with organising the Kragljivoda Territorial Defence. To your knowledge in June 1992, was Bektic involved in that?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that and I don't think that we should confuse things here because Kragljivoda and Karacici are two different things. They are about five to six kilometres away from one another. I don't know who was the leader of the group from Karacici but I know and I can claim that the group from Kragljivoda was led by Sefik Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I've finished with that document. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting; it's just a clarification. The previous answer the witness gave, he never heard of this what he says he never heard of the term Territorial Defence, it was a group from Osmace and so on, and the witness went on to say, that there were no military units, "it was a resistance organised by the population, there were no military units of any sort." I understand that the witness to be talking about Osmace but if he's not, and he's talking about a broader statement, then I think that should be clarified. Just in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. case my understanding is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're a hundred per cent right. Yes, Mr. Jones, could you address this matter to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think first I think we need to be clear which areas this witness can speak about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Obviously you know the situation in Osmace. Were you familiar with the situation in Kragljivoda in, let's say, June 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: The population came along a road. We did not have any actual links with Kragljivoda and they used to tell us that Sefik was the leader there because we did not actually have any actual contact with them, because we still continued. I mean, there was this road between Osmace and Kragljivoda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. It's simply this: Your statement that there were not units, organised military units, did that apply to Kragljivoda as well or are you only talking about Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Osmace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Thank you, Mr. Jones. And the witness. Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just before we leave this document, I would like to put a question directly here. If the witness perhaps would read this document once more in the first paragraph, it speaks of that all local leaders of self-organised armed groups are ordered to do this or that. So the document speaks of local, self-organised armed groups. Is it in the same sense as you spoke of self-organised groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just need to make a distinction here. Those were not armed groups as such because the resistance on the part of the population included people who were not armed as well. I mean, I did mention that we only had 21 rifles and there were about 50 of us in the group so not armed groups as such. There were about 50 men in that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document were to suggest that there were self-organised armed groups in Osmace and Kragljivoda, is that something which you would regard as accurate or inaccurate, as of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Let me continue. At Osmace, there was a group of about 50 men and they had about 20 rifles, and as to Kragljivoda, as I've been saying all along, as we heard later, Sefik had about 10 men, maximum. It was not actually in Kragljivoda itself. It was a forest called Kalina which is 2 or 3 kilometres away from Kragljivoda because nobody dared go anywhere near Kragljivoda even in June because the Serbs were in control of that road and they would often drive up in a Niva car and they would fire their arms, and at some point in mid-June, they torched the post office and shop that had already been destroyed before. So in the month of June, Serbs used to come to Kragljivoda and on one of those occasions, they torched the post office and the shop which is actually empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to some of the areas mentioned here later but for the time being I want to pass on to another subject. And still approaching events chronologically, you described how in May, 7th, 8th of May 1992, I think there was this torching of all of the Muslim villages in the Skelani area. I want to ask you about villages on the other side, along the Drina down from Bratunac towards Skelani. Did you hear of any goings on in those areas, in the Muslim villages n May 1992?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of May, in the morning, Serbs from Skelani started taking artillery to an elevation called Stolac. This is at a distance of about 2 to 3 kilometres from Osmace. So three to four buses full of Serb soldiers drove up, and they surrounded the village of Osmace, and they started shelling the village from all directions, from Stolac, from the Tara plateau in Serbia, from the Serb village of Brezani, and from the village of Ratkovici. And during a period of time of about three or four hours, they were shelling us so much that there was about 5.000 shells that landed there and so the entire population fled, and they escaped through Pasalidji [phoen] to Subin. They went through Korjen to Subin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I stop you there? Were you among that group of people?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you return to Osmace?

utterances.speaker: NESIB BURIC
